name.text: Classifying rational and irrational numbers from a given set

questiontext.text:
Consider the following six numbers and tick the box next to every number that is irrational.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

A number is rational if it can be written as a fraction \(\displaystyle \frac{p}{q}\) where \(p\) and \(q\) are integers and \(q \neq 0\) (its decimal expansion either terminates or repeats). A number is irrational if it cannot be written as a ratio of two integers.

Examine each of the six numbers:

  • \({@n1@}\) is a whole number (integer), which can be written as \(\displaystyle \frac{{@n1@}}{1}\), so it is rational.
  • \({@n2@}\) is already a ratio of two integers, so it is rational.
  • \(\sqrt{{@n3_sq@}}\) looks irrational because of the square root symbol, but \({@n3_sq@} = {@n3_root@}^2\) is a perfect square, so \(\sqrt{{@n3_sq@}} = {@n3_root@} = \displaystyle \frac{{@n3_root@}}{1}\) is rational.
  • \(\sqrt{{@n4_base@}}\) simplifies partially to \({@n4_simp@}\), which still contains an irrational square root because \({@n4_base@}\) is not a perfect square—so \(\sqrt{{@n4_base@}}\) is irrational.
  • \(\sqrt{{@n5_base@}}\) is irrational because \({@n5_base@}\) is not a perfect square, so \(\sqrt{{@n5_base@}}\) cannot be simplified to an integer or a fraction of integers.
  • \(\pi\) is irrational because its decimal expansion (\(3.14159\ldots\)) is non-terminating and non-repeating.

Key takeaway: Always simplify a number fully before deciding whether it is rational or irrational.

\(\displaystyle \boxed{ \text{Irrational numbers: } \sqrt{{@n4_base@}}, \; \sqrt{{@n5_base@}}, \; \pi }\)

node.description: Check exact set of irrational numbers
Check if student selected sqrt(n3_sq), which simplifies to an integer

truefeedback.text: You selected \(\sqrt{{@n3_sq@}}\), which is actually rational because \({@n3_sq@} = {@n3_root@}^2\) is a perfect square, so \(\sqrt{{@n3_sq@}} = {@n3_root@}\). Not every expression with a square root symbol is irrational.

node.description: Check if student selected a rational integer or fraction

truefeedback.text: Whole numbers and fractions of integers (such as \({@n1@}\) and \({@n2@}\)) can be written in the form \(\frac{p}{q}\), so they are rational, not irrational.

node.description: Check if student forgot to select pi

truefeedback.text: Remember to include \(\pi\): it is an irrational number because its decimal expansion is non-terminating and non-repeating.

falsefeedback.text: You correctly avoided the rational numbers, but your selection is incomplete. Tick all three irrational numbers: \(\sqrt{{@n4_base@}}\), \(\sqrt{{@n5_base@}}\), and \(\pi\).
